guide.headline: Jets defense tries to cage a Bears offense built on the ground
guide.hook: This is a slow bleed game, Jets secondary against Bears explosiveness and Bears run game against a shaky Jets front, with a rookie safety flying around the middle of it all.

items.title: Thieneman roams the Bears secondary
items.what: Dillon Thieneman is playing 100 percent of Bears defensive snaps as the No. 1 safety, and he is producing like a top-two pick despite being drafted at No. 25. He already has one interception, three pass breakups, and 15 tackles, top 5 percent production for an NFL safety.
items.when: Any time the Jets push the ball down the field or into the middle of the field.

items.title: Jets secondary caps the deep ball
items.what: The Jets are No. 1 of 32 in limiting explosive passes, allowing just 1.05 on that measure, while the Bears offense ranks a middling No. 16 at 1.34. That is a 48 percentile point gap, a clear defensive edge that should force Chicago to drive the long way.
items.when: Track the longest Bears completion by halftime.
items.who: Bears deep passing vs Jets secondary

items.title: Bears lean on the ground game
items.what: The Bears rush success rate sits at 41 percent, No. 15 of 32, and the Jets run defense ranks No. 26 at 46 percent allowed, a 36 percentile point gap in Chicago's favor. If the Bears stay committed, they keep third downs short and the clock moving.
items.when: Count Bears rushing attempts by halftime.
items.who: Bears run game vs Jets run defense

guide.cardLine: Watch a rookie safety roam center field while the Bears try to grind it out on the ground against a shaky Jets run defense.
